name: FPNMI
description: FPNMI (Feasibility Portability and Non-Transferability in Hardware-Aware Neural Architecture Search) is a reproducible research artifact accompanying the study of whether hardware-aware neural architecture search evidence transfers safely across deployment targets. This artifact evaluates the distinction between ranking portability, feasibility portability, and deployment authorization. It provides complete benchmark protocols, executable analysis code, provenance records, verification scripts, and frozen result files supporting large-scale evaluation across hardware targets. The artifact includes: HW-NAS evaluation evidence using the complete NAS-Bench-201 architecture space with target-specific hardware measurements. HW-GPT cross-device transfer analysis across 13 hardware devices, 156 ordered proxy–target relationships, and frozen joint-constraint regimes. Raw and derived benchmark outputs, including ranking analysis, feasibility-risk measurements, threshold sweeps, and closure summaries. Reproducibility infrastructure, including execution protocols, provenance metadata, artifact verification, and integrity manifests. The artifact supports investigation of a central deployment question: whether high correlation in architecture ranking is sufficient evidence for safe deployment under target-specific hard constraints.
